soundness_flags.label: ass:conditional-fourth-moment
soundness_flags.one_line: The Catoni2012 citation supports bounded variance or bounded standardized kurtosis, not the stated uniform conditional raw fourth-central-moment condition; retag this condition as novel with an applicability justification, or replace the citation/condition with the actual calibration hypothesis.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper analyzes robust mean/variance procedures under bounded variance or bounded variance together with bounded kurtosis; its Section 4 construction is parameterized by an upper bound on standardized kurtosis, not by a conditional raw fourth-central-moment envelope.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 9–10, Theorem 2; p. 27, Theorem 8 and following discussion; p. 39, Appendix C.5
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 2 lower-bounds squared error for the one-arm functional ψ1 at n⁻¹+d²/(n²log²n); Appendix C.5 sets μ0k=0 in its lower-bound construction; Appendix A states asymptotic normality also for d=o(√n).

Under its nuisance-rate, overlap, moment, and nondegeneracy conditions, Theorem 5.1 gives first-order equivalent DML ATE/ATTE estimators, normal limits, variance replacement, uniform asymptotic confidence validity, and efficiency for efficient scores.

The article studies ATE inference under unconfoundedness, obtains finite-sample optimal estimators and intervals under smoothness/shape restrictions with normal known-variance errors, and gives feasible asymptotic procedures for unknown errors.
The paper constructs simultaneous/selective confidence intervals for probabilities of individual unobserved multinomial outcomes, with a distinct missing-mass discussion.

The paper establishes Cramér-type moderate-deviation results for self-normalized processes, including Studentized U-statistics, rather than a theorem for pilot-selected growing-order factorial statistics.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make the fourth-moment premise bibliographically and mathematically exact: either use a bounded conditional kurtosis condition compatible with the intended Catoni score, or explicitly present the raw conditional fourth-moment envelope as the proposal's new calibration regime and prove why it suffices.

Sharpen the tail-calibration OEQ into a reproducible construction by fixing the block partition, influence transform, score, monotonicity argument, and all constants before the global interval theorem is advanced.

Add the now-published Painsky JASA treatment of confidence intervals for parameters of unobserved events as a deliberately orthogonal large-alphabet inference comparator, explaining why its selective coordinatewise target cannot yield an ATE interval.

recommended_next_step: Revise the fourth-moment assumption’s standard/novel status and calibration rationale, then advance the otherwise field-grade honest-length frontier to Stage 0.
